post_title: Padded, soft  shoulder pads
post_details: I suffered for a long time with standard shoulder pads from the library. Size position, then pinned them, lifted, lowered. Very time-consuming occupation. Then he remembered that we have 3D pen. 1. We draw the shoulder pad of the desired shape, immediately freeze, and lower not much into the body. (By default, there is a gap on the avatar and fabric. 2. Duplicate the layer from above, break the connection, remove the circular seam, and sew along 1 side, leaving the armhole slice not Stitched. 3. Correct the external line, raise the pressure 1-2. 4. Lay the internal line and set the fold about 100 degrees 5. Iron, pressure and fold the inner line. shoulder pads are working, soft, if necessary, you can raise lower pressure. I hope this will be useful.

post_title: HOW TO: Create & Save Custom Views for Presentations & Line Sheets
post_details: Hi All, Creating Custom Views for Rendering, Snapshots, &amp Presentations is pretty easy. They can also be saved and used again in any file. PART 1 SETTING UP MY CLO FILE FOR RENDERING 1. Hide Avatar (Shift + A) 2. Use the Hi-Res Garment Tool to make your 3D Garment high quality 3. High-Res Garment Settings These are my preferred settings, the defaults make the skin offset 0.0 (which I sometimes think can be too low and cause collision with the avatar). In addition, I un-check changing the Simulation quality because I'm using the fabric from the CLO Library and I don't plan on physically creating this garment - thus a more accurate version of the Simulation is unnecessary for me. 4. Simulate After boosting the resolution, you'll need to simulate the garment again to apply the changes. PART 2 CREATING AND RENDERING CUSTOM VIEWS Set Custom Views (Optional Addition - Check Views against render settings) For this example, since my renders are the most important part of the setup, I'm going to set my image output size before setting up my custom views. I'm going to render each view at 4"x6" @ 300 PPI 1. Open Render Preview Window 2. Start the Render Preview Click on the Render Window or Click the "Interactive Render" button to start the preview. 3. Set your Image Size 3a. Click on the Image/Video Properties Tool 3b. Change the Image Size to a Paper Preset 3c. Adjust to the size and resolution you want 4. Open the Custom View Window right-click in the 3D Window Background and select "Custom Views" 5. Create Views For this, I'm going to rely on my render preview, each time I have a view I like, I'll click the Custom View Camera Icon Pro Tip: If you hold SHIFT while you rotate, you will lock the vertical axis to avoid any accidental tilting. 6. Rename the Views I like to name views so they are easy to organize and open later. To rename the Views, double click / long click on the Custom_View_X name in your Custom View Menu. 7. Render All Custom Views To render all your Custom Views, navigate to your Image/Video Render Properties &gt Viewpoint &gt Custom Views 8. Render Change any other rendering / lighting settings (more info about rendering here, here, &amp here), and Click the "Final Render" Tool PART 3 REUSING CUSTOM VIEWS IN OTHER PRESENTATIONS 1. Save Custom Views In the Custom View Menu, click Save All. Navigate to the folder you want to save them to, and click Select Folder. 2. Add Views to other files Open other file (File &gt Open &gt Project Ctrl + O) Right-click in the 3D Window Background to Open the Custom View Menu. Then click the open button. 3. Select all views from the folder where you saved your custom views, and click "Open" 4. Views are in there &amp you can render them however you want or make adjustments just to this file! Good luck!

evoncassier, Under "User Settings" subsection 2D, there's a Notch option "Display Type". When "Length Fixed to Screen" is selected it's not possible to change the notch length. post_title: HOW TO : Import a color palette (.ase) from Illustrator into CLO
post_details: Hi all, If you want to import a color palette from a color card into CLO, here's how: 1. Open Color Card in Illustrator &amp Ensure your Swatch Palette is showing 2. Use the Black Arrow Selection Tool to select each color chip 3. In the swatch palette - click the icon for New Swatch to add it into your palette * if you already have swatches in there, select the first, hold shift and select the last swatch and click on the trash can icon to delete all the default swatches. 4. Name your swatch, and click OK 5. Once you have done this for all swatches, change your document color mode to RGB (this can be done anytime, I just often work in CMYK, so I do this right before I export the palette - your choice though) 6. In the Swatch Palette, use the menu extension to save your swatch library as an ASE file 7. Import into CLO Select the Fabric from the Object Browser &amp add the palette in the Property Editor. This color palette will remain in your program forever, until you manually delete it. In addition, it will appear for all color options (buttons, topstitching etc). Use the icons in the color palette editor to view &amp hide swatch names, or to change the size. Happy CLO-ing!

post_details: 현재 colorway 작업을 한 후 obj export를 하게 되면, mtl 파일은 colorway 창에 작업물 순서대로 "파일명_#.mtl" 형식으로 numbering되어 export 됩니다. (CLO v.4.2.242) *참고 이미지 : 예시 스크린 샷* Feedback - 문제/불편한 점 : 작업자가 colorway 순서를 인지하고 있지 않으면, export 결과물에서 직관적으로 작업한 colorway와 매칭되는 mtl 파일을 알아차리기 어렵습니다. (썸네일 이미지를 추출한 경우에도 썸네일 이미지에 매칭되는 mtl 파일을 알아차릴 수 없습니다.) - 희망하는 개선 내용 : 1. export 되는 mtl 파일명이 사용자가 지정한 colorway명으로 설정 되도록 개선 되거나, ( 스크린샷 기준 Example ) PaddingColor_0.mtl =&gt Colorway_A, PaddingColor_1.mtl =&gt Colorway_B ....... 2. colorway와 mtl 매칭 정보를 json형식으로 제공해 주도록 개선되면, export 결과물 만으로도 각 colorway에 해당하는 mtl파일을 매칭하는데 좋을 것으로 보입니다. - 부가 의문 사항 : export 시 CLO 작업창에 현재 3D창에 있는 모델의 Colorway의 mtl이 numbering이 붙지 않는 "파일명.mtl"(스크린 샷 기준 PaddingColor.mtl) 형태로 중복해서 export됩니다. 현재 작업창에 있는 모델의mtl을 별도로 중복되게 export 되게하는 다른 이유가 있는지, 이 부분도 개선 가능한지 궁금합니다. 감사합니다.

post_title: Expressing Trims using Topstitch
post_details: Hi Everyone, Just wanted to share some different ways you can customize the topstitch tool! In my examples I applied texture images for Swarovski crystals, trim tape, grosgrain or just a simple binding. See below the sizes I used and how I cropped the images: All you need to do to create custom topstitches is select a topstitch in the Object Browser and locate it's Property Editor. Then change the "Type" to Texture and simply import your image you wish to repeat. Topstitch can be applied to pattern edges and also internal lines, which makes it handy to quickly apply trims or mock up style lines/binding. See below for the settings to look out for: For the red binding, I simply created a small rectangular repeat particularly for curved lines. When you create your own, you may notice small gaps in between the repeated graphic as it follows any sort of curved lines. You can adjust the topstitch spacing to -.1 and it should close the gap. The thinner your texture is the more seamless your repeat will be! People all always curious how to quickly visualize binding, particularly for sportswear rather than create thin pattern pieces to sew onto a garment. I find this to be a nice alternative! You can always add normal maps and apply fabric types to the topstitch for added effects/realism. See working window vs. render below: Hope some of you find inspiration from this!

post_title: Actual Working Snaps instead of Buttons
post_details: It seems like the only solution today to create a snap closure (like a placket) is to fake it by choosing snaps from the button options and sewing the placket closed. If you want the closure to actually work you have to also choose buttonholes and link the button (snap) and buttonhole. But this doesn't look realistic if you want the snap closure look realistic without buttonholes. I suggest either adding a separate section for snap closures (male and female) and allowing the snaps to be linked in lieu of choosing a button and buttonhole. Or keep the button and buttonhole category as it exists today but add the male snaps to buttons and female snaps to buttonholes. This dress is just an example of what I am trying to acheive. Today when I try this on the right side placket I have chosen buttons that look like snaps, but on the left side placket I must choose buttonholes in order to link the two to close the placket. Other option is to attached buttons that look like snaps on both sides of the placket and sew the placket closed.
